description:
Finding: crates/smtp/src/sieve_admin.rs lines 38-45 define a private fn is_loopback_addr(addr: &str) -> bool that is byte-for-byte identical to stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr. The shared version already exists and is imported by other callers (reader/config.rs line 4, transit/config.rs line 8, mail/main.rs line 3). sieve_admin.rs does not import stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr — it reimplements it locally.

Risk: If the loopback detection logic is ever fixed (e.g. to handle '::ffff:127.0.0.1' IPv4-mapped addresses, or 'ip6-localhost'), the fix applied to stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr will not automatically propagate to the sieve_admin copy. The sieve admin endpoint will silently use the old logic. The divergence is invisible to grep searches for 'is_loopback_addr' because the local fn has the same name but is a different definition.

Suggested fix: Remove the local fn is_loopback_addr in sieve_admin.rs and replace it with use stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr at the top of the file (or call stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr directly). stoa-smtp already depends on stoa_core, so no new dependency is needed.
title: sieve_admin.rs contains a private copy of is_loopback_addr
